title: Saka settles gruelling battle with Aston Villa to extend Arsenal’s winning start
author: Ben Fisher
content:
The smile on Declan Rice’s face a few minutes from time said it all. The Arsenal midfielder had just shut down Ian Maatsen as the Aston Villa full-back zoomed into the box. Arsenal were hardly imperious, Bukayo Saka scoring the only goal, but Unai Emery’s side struggled to hurt the champions, David Raya untroubled. The records will show Villa have lost their first two league matches of a season without scoring for the first time since 2002 but, despite successive defeats, this time there was no capitulation.
For Villa, this was a marked improvement on defeat at Brighton in their opener. After 31 minutes in their last game, they trailed 4-0 and after 40 were down to 10 men. Here they could take plenty of encouragement from a promising first-half performance, the debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson impressing, having taken the Nos 1 and 11 vacated by Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins respectively. Suzuki’s eye for a pass was particularly noticeable, pinging 50-yard balls to the 19-year-old George Hemmings and John McGinn, the pair operating on opposite flanks.
Suzuki and Jackson were the only changes to Villa’s starting XI but they appeared far more cohesive, Ross Barkley partnering Boubacar Kamara at the base of midfield. Emi Buendía smacked the crossbar after Kamara overawed Christos Tzolis – Martin Ødegaard subsequently asked questions of the referee, Jarred Gillett – but Jackson otherwise created Villa’s best opening. The Senegal forward, who worked under Emery at Villarreal, pinched possession from Gabriel Magalhães a few yards into the Villa half and galloped into the other before sending in a near-perfect cross from the right. Hemmings burst into the six-yard box but was unable to convert. How Villa welcomed having an orthodox striker on the pitch after Watkins’s omission at Brighton.
This was an advert for a new-look Villa, on and off the pitch. A handful of staff in hard hats were positioned in the closed North Stand moonlighting as ball boys; the corner of rubble between the remaining skeleton and the Trinity Road Stand is akin to an excavation site. Ibrahim Mbaye, whose £47m move from Paris Saint-Germain is to be announced on Tuesday, was in the directors’ box. Six of Villa’s starting XI from their Europa League triumph may have departed but Emery has made no complaints and has relayed his no-excuses mantra to his squad. “We do not look backwards,” Villa’s manager said in the buildup.
“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that,” crowed Villa’s supporters as Arsenal players huddled before kick-off close to the visiting support. Ezri Konsa was on the bench on his return to Villa Park and received a warm welcome as he headed for the away dugout. Suzuki grew into the game, his first action of note failing to claim the ball at a corner, allowing Gabriel to send a header off target. Up the other end Kai Havertz sent a shot wide after a neat pass from Ødegaard at the end of an intricate move, though the Arsenal forward was offside. Matty Cash largely muted Tzolis, such an influence in Arsenal’s previous matches.
Tzolis got little change out of Cash and was booked for bringing him down after the Villa full-back snatched the ball. Cash celebrated winning the free-kick by revving up the home crowd, the stadium’s capacity down to 37,000. Cash had to focus on marking a different opponent in the second half and Tzolis’s replacement, Eberechi Eze, was involved in Arsenal seizing the lead approaching the hour. Arsenal slowed things down and then came alive, punishing Villa for switching off. Cristhian Mosquera pushed a pass to Eze, who Cash afforded space, Villa’s defender concerned about an unmarked Riccardo Calafiori. Eze promptly spied Calafiori’s underlapping run and the Italian steered the ball across the six-yard box, where Saka beat Maatsen to the punch and scrambled the cross into the net.
![Zion Suzuki, Aston Villa’s new goalkeeper, applauds the home fans after the final whistle](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/ac45edb42820124314e760cb3f89a80ac8b9c722/0_0_3458_2306/master/3458.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Five minutes earlier Villa survived a scare. Maatsen clipped Saka’s heels as the winger raced on to Declan Rice’s through ball and Gillett initially awarded a penalty. But a VAR review showed the foul was outside the area and soon the Arsenal players in lemon yellow gathered by the spot moseyed towards the edge of Villa’s 18-yard box. Ødegaard sent the free-kick into the side netting. Mikel Merino and Bruno Guimarães arrived from the bench as Villa pushed for an equaliser. Up the other end Suzuki made a mess of a routine save from Havertz but almost instantly made amends, diverting Havertz’s shot wide after the forward, subsequently flagged offside, was released on goal.
after newsletter promotion
Villa’s frustrations were palpable. McGinn, in a hurry to get Villa level, was booked for wiping out Merino. Aaron Wan-Bissaka replaced Cash for his Villa debut, his first job to stretch his legs and muffle an advancing Eze. Alejandro Garnacho entered in place of Barkley. Arteta, too, changed personnel, Konsa coming on for his debut for Mosquera. Villa could not find a way past Arsenal, whose winning habit already appears ominous.
summary: Bukayo Saka scored the only goal of the match to secure a hard-fought victory for Arsenal against Aston Villa, extending their winning start to the season. Despite the defeat, Villa showed a marked improvement from their opening-match loss, delivering a cohesive performance that included promising debuts from Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson. Arsenal ultimately held firm to claim all three points, leaving Villa without a goal or a point in their first two league matches.
key_points: Bukayo Saka scored the game's sole goal near the hour mark, converting a cross from Riccardo Calafiori.
Aston Villa showed significant improvement compared to their opening-match defeat against Brighton, despite losing their first two league games without scoring for the first time since 2002.
New signings Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson made impressive debuts for Aston Villa.
Arsenal's defence remained untroubled as they successfully protected their narrow lead until the final whistle.

title: Barcola completes Â£123m Liverpool move
author: Alex Brotherton; Mohamed Moallim
content:
![Bradley Barcola](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/873/cpsprodpb/04a8/live/705dce60-a53d-11f1-a492-cfe8e2df591b.jpg)
Barcola made 152 appearances in all competitions for PSG
- Published
Liverpool have completed the signing of France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee worth up to Â£123m.
PSG initially valued the 23-year-old at Â£145m, but Liverpool will pay an initial Â£106m plus Â£17m in potential add-ons.
Barcola has signed a five-year contract to become the fifth new arrival at Anfield this summer, following the signings of winger Victor Munoz and defenders Jeremy Jacquet, Ronald Araujo and Ifeanyi Ndukwe.
"It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play," Barcola said.
"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League - it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.
"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term - that's why I signed a long contract â and I hope I can do it."
Barcola, who will wear the number 29 shirt at Anfield, prefers to play on the left wing but can operate across the forward line.
The France international will add depth to Andoni Iraola's squad following the departure of Mohamed Salah, the long-term injury absence of Hugo Ekitike, and the potential sale of Cody Gakpo.
Last season, Barcola scored 13 goals and provided seven assists in 49 games in all competitions for PSG.
He featured in all eight of France's games at the 2026 World Cup, scoring three goals as Les Bleus reached the third-place play-off.
Barcola joined PSG from Lyon in 2023 for a reported Â£38.5m and won three Ligue 1 titles, two Champions Leagues, the French Cup twice, the Uefa Super Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.
The fee Liverpool have agreed to pay includes covering a solidarity payment PSG owe Lyon as part of the deal that took Barcola to Paris three years ago.
The stats that show Barcola's strengths
Barcola is a left winger by trade, having played almost all of his Champions League minutes for PSG on that flank, but his game is shaped by a centre-forward's instincts. He played as a striker until the age of 17, something reflected in his movement and shot selection.
Last season, he averaged 3.5 shots per 90 minutes in Ligue 1, placing him among the division's most active shooters despite operating from wide areas.
His 9.83 expected goals (xG) ranked in the 95th percentile among wingers across Europe's top five leagues, meaning only around 5% of wide players consistently found themselves in better goalscoring positions.
Barcola converted those chances into 11 league goals, outperforming his xG, while no PSG player or Ligue 1 winger recorded a higher xG total during the 2025-26 campaign.
Those instincts are reflected in how he attacks defenders. Barcola was the only player across Europe's top five leagues to average more than two shot-ending carries per 90 minutes (2.06), illustrating his ability to drive at opponents before creating shooting opportunities for himself.
He also averaged 8.69 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes - the seventh-highest figure among more than 1,500 eligible players - reinforcing the profile of a winger who consistently occupies goalscoring positions.
His shot map highlights a player who attacks dangerous central areas rather than settling for speculative efforts from distance. Only Ousmane Dembele had a better combined shot volume with chance creation in Ligue 1, underlining Barcola's rare ability to both finish attacks and create opportunities for team-mates.
His work without the ball is another reason Liverpool's recruitment team admired him. Barcola ranked ninth across Europe's top five leagues for possessions won in the final third last season, a metric that reflects the aggressive pressing and intensity demanded under Andoni Iraola.
summary: Liverpool have completed the signing of France forward Bradley Barcola from Paris St-Germain for a fee worth up to £123m. The 23-year-old has signed a five-year contract to become the fifth new arrival at Anfield this summer. Barcola scored 13 goals and provided seven assists in 49 games for PSG last season and aims to help Liverpool win the Premier League.
key_points: Liverpool signed Bradley Barcola for an initial £106m plus £17m in potential add-ons.
Barcola agreed to a five-year contract and will wear the number 29 shirt.
He joins following the departure of Mohamed Salah, the injury absence of Hugo Ekitike, and potential sale of Cody Gakpo.
Last season for PSG, he recorded 13 goals and seven assists across 49 appearances in all competitions.

title: Ailing Novak Djokovic falls in US Open first round for earliest grand slam exit in 20 years
author: Tumaini Carayol
content:
The first night session of the US Open this year was approaching the three-hour mark when Novak Djokovic walked briskly to the corner of the vast Arthur Ashe Stadium court, bent down and vomited the contents of his stomach straight into the towel bin.
This was neither the first nor the last time that Djokovic threw up during an excruciating four hours and 36 minutes of suffering, and his miserable night ended around midnight with the 24-time grand slam champion in tears as he was defeated 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 by Mariano Navone in the first round.
Djokovic’s appearance here marked a record-extending 84th outing at a grand slam tournament but it produced one of his most abject defeats. This is just the third time in the 39-year-old’s career that he has lost in the first round of a major and the first time he has done so since the 2006 Australian Open, over 20 years ago, when he was 18 years old. Perhaps the most startling part of this loss was how early Djokovic’s suffering had started. Before he had even consolidated his opening break at 2-0 in the first set, barely 15 minutes into the match, Djokovic already appeared to be struggling with the humidity even though the match was played in less extreme night-time conditions.
Over the course of the subsequent five sets, Djokovic appeared to be in a daze on the court, alternating between panting desperately from behind the baseline, vomiting, struggling to find his balance and fighting off cramps. By the end of the match, he had nothing left to give.
This was not merely an unlucky illness that struck Djokovic at an inopportune time. Just a couple of weeks ago at the Cincinnati Open, Djokovic struggled badly in similar evening humidity against another Argentinian opponent who did not appear to have any issues in the conditions, with Thiago Agustín Tirante defeating Djokovic in three sets.
Afterwards, Djokovic said that a particular health condition, accentuated by the heat and humidity, was behind his physical struggles. He reiterated those sentiments after this latest painful loss. “I think it was obvious that [it was] an awful feeling on the court for me,” Djokovic said. “It is something that I’ve been carrying, unfortunately, pretty much every match this year. You know, vomiting, throwing up, serious issue there, and then my whole body starts to collapse, basically cramping and pain, and the back just gave up in the end, and shoulder, and I couldn’t close it out, break up in the fourth, but just struggled all the way since the fourth game of the match. And again, don’t want to take too much out of his win. Congrats to him; he’s a nice guy, fighter, but you know, I didn’t enjoy myself.”
![Djokovic tries to cool down during a break in play.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/3d33c1121e13d8f6773a66d829ae5fd31ffb7a97/0_0_2557_1707/master/2557.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Although Navone is a tough competitor who has impressively re-established himself inside the top 50 after nearly exiting the top 100 last year, nearly all of his best results had come on clay. This was, on paper, a kind first-round draw for Djokovic and seemingly a chance for him to start his tournament quickly and conserve energy.
Instead, it took just 20 minutes for the drama to begin. Midway through the first set, Djokovic began to cough and splutter from behind the baseline, repeatedly bending over. At 4-3, rain led the tournament organisers to close the Arthur Ashe Stadium roof.
From that point until the end of the match, this was an uncomfortable spectacle. While Navone looked completely unaffected by the conditions, Djokovic lathered himself with ice cloths to cool down, and at 5-4 in the opening set, the doctor provided him with pills. Despite his struggles, Djokovic served great for a large part of the match, which allowed him to hang on for so long.
![Navone celebrates the biggest win of his career.](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/aea8d118a954f065b9169dd316667834e870ca4d/0_0_3696_2464/master/3696.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Navone, meanwhile, has long dreamed of a moment like this. The 25-year-old considers Djokovic his idol, and not long after the draw was revealed, fans uncovered proof of his fandom in the form of a 13-year-old Navone’s tweets from 2014. A large number of Navone’s old tweets on his X account were devoted to supporting Djokovic. His parents had not planned to attend the US Open this year, but the draw forced them to abort their Caribbean holiday and fly to New York.
On the most significant occasion of Navone’s career, he played a good match, chasing down every ball, maintaining immaculate length off both wings and forcing Djokovic into bruising extended exchanges that the Serb was in no condition to handle. However, Djokovic spent most of the night barely hanging on. He vomited numerous times throughout the match and by the fourth set he started to fight off cramps. Djokovic’s brilliant serving and eternal fight kept him alive for much of his time on court and he established a two sets to one lead with a break in set four. By the fourth set, however, his legs were heavy and his first serve deteriorated. Not long after that, Djokovic was walking off the court and back to the locker room in tears, having suffered another brutal reminder of the difficulties of competing at the highest level at such an advanced age.
summary: Novak Djokovic suffered a stunning first-round exit at the US Open, losing in five sets to Mariano Navone after battling severe physical illness, vomiting, and cramping. The 24-time grand slam champion attributed his collapse to an ongoing health condition exacerbated by heat and humidity. This defeat marks just the third first-round major loss of his career and his earliest grand slam exit in 20 years.
key_points: Novak Djokovic was defeated by Mariano Navone 7-6 (5), 5-7, 4-6, 6-2, 6-1 in the first round of the US Open.
Djokovic suffered from repeated vomiting, cramps, and physical exhaustion throughout the four-hour and 36-minute match.
Djokovic stated that he has been dealing with this recurring health issue during matches throughout the year.
This is only the third first-round grand slam exit of Djokovic's career and his earliest major exit since the 2006 Australian Open.
Navone, who idolized Djokovic growing up, played a consistent match and capitalized on Djokovic's physical collapse to secure the biggest win of his career.

title: ‘Amazing’ Itauma urged not to give up by Hrgovic after stunning stoppage
author: Donald McRae
content:
Moses Itauma has been urged “not to give up” by Filip Hrgovic, the new IBF world heavyweight champion, who stopped the 21-year-old Briton with a dramatic and stunning turnaround in their title fight late on Saturday night at London’s O2 Arena.
Itauma was taken to hospital in a precautionary measure after the fight and Frank Warren, his promoter, confirmed to the Guardian on Sunday morning that his young heavyweight was still under medical observation.
“He’s still in hospital, still under observation,” Warren said of Itauma. “I think they’ll let him out today. They’re just doing the usual tests because he didn’t get there until late. So he got some sleep and they’re just doing what they normally do. He should be okay. I’ve messaged him a couple of times. He’s messaged back. We’ll have a call later today.”
Hrgovic said he had lost the first eight rounds to the “amazing” Itauma, whom he also described as “the best guy in the division, the most talented guy in the division”, but that his own hard-bitten experience after nine years as a professional fighter was the telling difference.
The 34-year-old Croat also stressed that Itauma made some basic mistakes in the pacing of the fight and, for all his speed and skill, ended up brawling like an amateur in the last two tumultuous rounds of a gripping battle. “My advice is to, of course, not give up,” Hrgovic said of Itauma, “not lose his confidence, to get a few easy fights, easy wins, to build again, and to learn from these mistakes. You can’t box like an amateur. It’s a 12-round fight, man. You need to pace yourself. You need to, in every moment, be ready and, you know, it’s a marathon. It’s not a sprint.”
Asked if it had always been his plan to take the bout into the later rounds, Hrgovic shook his head. “No, I thought I’m gonna connect more from the beginning, but I couldn’t match his speed. He’s very fast. I didn’t see his punches coming. I didn’t see his counters coming. I thought it was gonna be easier but I just couldn’t land.”
Hrgovic pointed to the inexperience of Itauma which cost him at such a crucial period after he had built a wide lead on the scorecards. “He’s just a kid. He could have boxed [at range] for the last few rounds. Use his legs, box. He was winning all the rounds. But he went toe-to-toe with me in round [nine]. It was a stupid move from him. Very stupid. But it’s inexperience. He’s an amazing fighter, but he’s still young.”
Itauma left the ring on a stretcher, after being given oxygen. At the post-fight press conference Warren said: “It’s precautionary that he’s gone to the hospital. That’s what we always do, because the most important thing is the boxer’s health.”
The promoter added: “He’s done something to his leg as well and he was quite tired. It was a high-paced, fast fight for both guys.” Warren, who also promotes Hrgovic, praised the Croat as a “classy guy, a classy champ. He’s been really honest about how hard the fight was for him too.”
after newsletter promotion
The weary but happy new champion spoke of how, over the years, “God tested me many times, and I endure everything. I stay strong, and he now gave me the best possible gift to win a world title against the best guy in the division, the most talented guy in the division. And there is no better way for me to become a world champion.”
![Filip Hrgovic poses for a photo with his IBF world heavyweight belt](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/2149f0ecee23e6f8db50269f78adf8c4964e69e2/0_0_5426_3665/master/5426.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
He offered one more note of advice for his vanquished young rival. “He’s really fast but I didn’t feel his power. He needs to work on his power to sit more on his punches. When he knocked me down [in the second round] I wasn’t hurt. I just didn’t see the punches coming. But he needs to pace himself. He needs to adjust a little bit to professional boxing. He’s definitely an amazing talent, and I believe he’ll be world champion for sure. But he needs more time.”
summary: Filip Hrgovic stopped 21-year-old Moses Itauma in a dramatic late-round turnaround at London's O2 Arena to claim the IBF world heavyweight title. Itauma was taken to the hospital as a precautionary measure for medical observation following the high-paced bout. Hrgovic praised the young Briton as the most talented fighter in the division but attributed the victory to his own experience and Itauma's tactical mistakes.
key_points: Filip Hrgovic defeated Moses Itauma by a stunning stoppage to become the new IBF world heavyweight champion.
Moses Itauma was taken to the hospital for precautionary medical observations after the fight.
Hrgovic admitted he lost the first eight rounds before capitalizing on Itauma's inexperience and pacing errors in the later rounds.
Promoter Frank Warren confirmed Itauma was expected to be released from the hospital after undergoing routine tests.
Hrgovic urged Itauma not to give up, expressing confidence that the young fighter will eventually become a world champion.

title: Moses Itauma says he will "be back" after world-title defeat by Filip Hrgovic
author: Alastair Telfer
content:
Highlights: Itauma misses out on world title after defeat by Hrgovic
- Published
Moses Itauma vowed "I'll be back" after failing in his attempt to become the second-youngest ever heavyweight world champion on Saturday.
Britain's Itauma, 21, tore through his first 14 opponents but his team threw in the towel in the ninth round against Filip Hrgovic at O2 Arena, London.
Having appeared to punch himself out, Itauma was barely able to stand as Hrgovic, 34, applied pressure to end the fight.
"It wasn't my night, we attempted greatness and just fell short to the more experienced man," Itauma said on social media.
"I want to say congratulations to Filip Hrgovic on his win. And although I never reached my desired outcome, I believe I gained experience that I'll take to my future fights.
"God bless, take care and I'll be back."
The vacant IBF title was on the line and Itauma was the favourite heading into the fight.
Hrgovic - who has lost only one professional fight, to Daniel Dubois in 2024 - is known for his durability, but he struggled to keep pace with Itauma early on.
However, his experience eventually told as the Briton was forced to leave the arena on a stretcher.
He was then taken to hospital and released overnight after having precautionary medical checks.
Queensberry Promotions boss Frank Warren believes Itauma needs a tactical rethink if he is to reach the top.
"That aura of invincibility, at the moment, is gone," Warren said. "People will look at that and maybe it will make it easier to make fights for him.
"He's still one of the most unbelievable talents I've ever been involved with. We'll stick with him. He needs a bit more ring craft and needs to stop thinking about knocking everyone out."
summary: Moses Itauma suffered his first defeat after his team threw in the towel in the ninth round of his world-title bout against Filip Hrgovic at London's O2 Arena. The 21-year-old Briton was attempting to become the second-youngest ever heavyweight world champion for the vacant IBF title. Following the bout, Itauma was taken to the hospital on a stretcher for precautionary checks before being released overnight.
key_points: Moses Itauma lost his world-title fight against Filip Hrgovic via a ninth-round stoppage after his corner threw in the towel.
The 21-year-old Briton was fighting for the vacant IBF heavyweight title at the O2 Arena in London.
Itauma was taken to the hospital on a stretcher for precautionary checks and was released overnight.
Promoter Frank Warren stated that Itauma needs to develop more ring craft and rethink his tactical approach following the defeat.

title: Man Utd 5-2 Ipswich: Bruno Fernandes scores hat-trick to help United come from behind to win at Old Trafford
author: Adam Bate
content:
Man Utd 5-2 Ipswich: Bruno Fernandes scores hat-trick to help United come from behind to win at Old Trafford
Report and free match highlights as Manchester United beat Ipswich Town 5-2 at Old Trafford; Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick helps Michael Carrick’s side bounce back from defeat to Hull on the opening weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side had led the game early on
Sunday 30 August 2026 20:15, UK
Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick as Manchester United came from behind to beat Ipswich 5-2 at Old Trafford and pick up their first win of the season.
It looked like being a difficult afternoon for Michael Carrick's team early on. Julio Enciso and Daizen Maeda both forced smart stops from Senne Lammens before Abdul Fatawu skinned Luke Shaw and fed Leif Davis to side-foot the opener high into the United net.
Old Trafford was edgy at that point, with United having lost to Hull on the opening weekend. But the game turned when Marcelino Nunez slipped over. Matheus Cunha robbed the Chilean midfielder and found Fernandes, who slammed the ball home with his left foot.

- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract📺
Bryan Mbeumo should have completed the turnaround early in the second half only to strike the bar from close range, but United did not have to wait long. Their second was not without controversy, however, as Harry Maguire escaped punishment for a handball.
Had his shot gone straight into the net then it would have been disallowed but because the attempt was diverted in by Jacob Greaves, it was allowed to stand. Moments later, United took the game away from Ipswich as Greaves' unfortunate afternoon continued.
The defender brought down Cunha when he was through on goal, and Fernandes, who had missed twice from the spot during pre-season, converted the penalty. It was party time thereafter, with Fernandes completing his hat-trick by slotting home in the 68th minute.
The skipper was not done. A wedged pass in behind found Mbeumo, who lobbed the goalkeeper to make it five. As the rain came down, Ipswich did pull one back in stoppage time through substitute Chuba Akpom but it was far too little and far too late.
With academy graduates Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in the starting line-up - in Rashford's case, for the first time since 2024 - there was a real mood of optimism inside the stadium at the end. Not perfect. But Manchester United's firepower is clear.
The key moments from Old Trafford
29 - GOAL! Fatawu skins Shaw and Davis finishes high into the net
40 - GOAL! Nunez slips and Cunha feeds Fernandes to equalise
52 - BAR! Mbeumo volleys against the bar from close range
56 - GOAL! Maguire's shot is deflected into his own net by Greaves
61 - GOAL! Fernandes converts a penalty after Cunha is fouled
68 - GOAL! Fernandes slots home to complete his hat-trick
82 - GOAL! Fernandes puts Mbeumo through to lob the keeper
90+1 - GOAL! Consolation as Martinez is robbed and Akpom scores
What do IFAB say on the handball?
It is an offence if a player scores in the opponents' goal:
- Directly from their hand/arm, even if accidental, including by the goalkeeper
- Immediately after the ball has touched their hand/arm, even if accidental
Following an accidental handball by the attacker:
- If the ball is clearly moving wide of the goal but is touched/played by a defending player and a clear own goal occurs, the goal should be awarded.
Fernandes stars again for Man Utd
"Without a shadow of a doubt, United's best signing in the post-Ferguson era," said Gary Neville on co-commentary for Sky Sports. No need for the caveat, really. This is one of the great Manchester United signings and one of the great Manchester United players.
There has been a bit of chatter about Bruno Fernandes recently given that he cleaned up with the awards for last season, adding the PFA prize to his FWA award. But this performance was a timely reminder that there is no better player in the Premier League.
Three goals and an assist when United needed him. And they do always seem to need him. It is the mentality as well as the magic in his boots. Amusingly, he was furious with himself in the 89th minute when an outside-of-the-boot cross failed to beat the first man.
Had Fernandes scored with one outrageous attempt from inside the centre-circle before that, then it really would have been a truly great display to remember. As it is, he had to settle for merely being the match-winner yet again. United's talisman.
Carrick: We have not cracked it!
Man Utd head coach Michael Carrick speaking to Sky Sports:
"We'll take a few more of them [hat-tricks]. He showed his quality today. Through the middle of the pitch, particularly Youri, Kobbi and Matheus played some really good football.
"Bruno's done what he's good at. He's won awards this week and bounced back from last week. Three goals, fantastic performance.
"We're not getting carried away. We weren't overly down last week, everything wasn't wrong. It was something we can improve on. Today, there are still things we can get better at.
"The result was great. We haven't cracked it, there's a long way to go and we'll get ready for next week."
O'Neil: Ipswich must respond better
Ipswich boss Gary O'Neil speaking to Sky Sports:
"To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford, you need the moments to go in your favour. They didn't. A couple went against us, and then we weren't good enough in the end for the last half-hour to get a hold of the game and make it look how it did at the start.
"We lost control of the momentum. That's the bit we'll focus on, really, trying to improve that because it can happen. People can slip, referees can make decisions, rules can go against you, or there can be a deflection.
"There are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control. It's then how we respond to that for the last half-hour that we need to get better at."
summary: Manchester United bounced back from their opening-weekend defeat by beating Ipswich Town 5-2 at Old Trafford. Bruno Fernandes led the victory with a hat-trick and an assist, helping Michael Carrick's side secure their first win of the season after falling behind early to Leif Davis's opener. Goals from Harry Maguire—via a deflection—and Bryan Mbeumo completed the scoring, with Ipswich adding a late consolation through Chuba Akpom.
key_points: Bruno Fernandes scored a hat-trick and provided an assist to lead Manchester United to a 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town.
Ipswich took an early lead through Leif Davis before United came from behind.
Harry Maguire benefited from a deflection off Jacob Greaves for United's second goal following a controversial handball appeal.
Bryan Mbeumo scored United's fifth goal after being set up by Fernandes.
Chuba Akpom scored a stoppage-time consolation goal for Ipswich.

title: Man Utd v Ipswich player ratings: Bruno Fernandes stars in Red Devils win
author: Simon Stone
content:
![Manchester United beat Ipswich 5-1 on Sunday](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/819/cpsprodpb/aacd/live/a03a36f0-a498-11f1-837c-8514728b4183.jpg)
Manchester United beat Ipswich 5-2 on Sunday
- Published
Manchester United
Senne Lammens: Stood firm and came out on top as Enciso charged at him. Out of his area to control and lay off a pass to Shaw at one point. 8
Diogo Dalot: So close to a rare goal with a curling left-footed effort. Defensively solid. 7
Harry Maguire: Reliable presence at the heart of the home defence, then got lucky with the deflection, otherwise his 'goal' might have been ruled out. 8
Lisandro Martinez: Experience vital on a day when the home side might have buckled. Mistake for Ipswich's late goal. 6
Luke Shaw: A difficult day for the England full-back. Struggled to deal with Fatawu. 5
Kobbie Mainoo: Restored to the starting line-up and good as ever on the ball. But United's midfield struggled to cope with Ipswich running at them. 6
Youri Tielemans: Still to find form in a Man Utd shirt. Went down too easily in the penalty area. Not secure defensively. 5
Bryan Mbeumo: Held his wide position and threatened with crosses and short passes. Unlucky Rashford's cross was deflected as he hit the bar from close range. Got his goal at the end. 6
Bruno Fernandes: Hat-trick hero. Sensational performance from the captain. Thunderous equaliser, kept his nerve with the penalty after two pre-season failures and calm third. Almost scored an outrageous fourth from halfway. 10
Marcus Rashford: First league start for Man Utd since December 2024. Got on the ball often enough and ran at the visitors' defence. Almost created a goal for Mbeumo. 7
Matheus Cunha: Began through the middle again and alternated with Fernandes as the furthest player forward. Decent. 7
Subs:
Leny Yoro (on 72, for Dalot): 6
Noussair Mazraoui (on 72, for Shaw): 6
Benjamin Sesko (79, for Cunha): 6
Patrick Dorgu (79, for Rashford): 7
Andrey Santos (79, for Mainoo): 6

Ipswich
Kjell Scherpen: Superb save to deny Dalot the opener and crucial touch to deny Mbeumo an easy finish. No chance with the equaliser. 8
Dara O'Shea: Robust defensive display and did well, until Fernandes took control. 6
Issa Diop: Lot of scrambling defence for the former West Ham man but coped OK for the most part and talked the Ipswich rearguard through the game. 6
Jacob Greaves: Composed on the ball and held his position, not getting drawn out when Cunha dropped deep. Probably lacked a bit of class at this level. 6
Leif Davis: Superb pass inside Dalot to release Maeda created one good chance for the visitors. Precise execution for his goal and might have had another. 8
Marcelino Nunez: Busy, in front of defence, wants to get on ball and slot in between centre-halves. Disastrous slip at just the wrong time let Man Utd in for crucial equaliser. 6
Sasa Lukic: Excellent addition to Ipswich ranks. Had the game nous to halt the home side's momentum, even at the expense of a yellow card. 7
Abdul Fatawu: Skinned Shaw close to the touchline and then had the awareness to pick out a team-mate as Ipswich took the lead. Booked for a poor tackle on Mbeumo but overall really good. 7
Julio Ensico: Held off Shaw and Mbeumo on length-of-field run but no reward as effort lacked power. A real threat. 8
Daizan Maeda: Good early raid down the left was early sign of Ipswich intentions. Shot from angle of area threatened home goal. 7
Emersonn: Tried use his size to pin Maguire and Martinez back and relished the physical tussle with the England man. 6

Marcus Rashford made his first league start for Manchester United since December 2024.

title: Chelsea v Brighton: How the players rated
author: Nizaar Kinsella
content:
![Joao Pedro points at the World Champions badge of Chelsea's shirt](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/970/cpsprodpb/6e9a/live/2215c980-a478-11f1-bed8-470734b5b662.jpg)
Joao Pedro scored for both teams in a thrilling match
- Published
Cole Palmer scored what turned out to be the decisive goal in a thrilling 4-3 victory for Chelsea over Brighton at Stamford Bridge.
Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto and Joao Pedro put the Blues 3-0 up, but Brighton reduced the deficit to a single goal through Malick Yalcouye and a Joao Pedro own goal before Palmer made it four. Pascal Gross then headed in a 96th-minute consolation goal after a dangerous long throw-in was not dealt with.
Here's how I rated the players, and how you rated them.
Chelsea
Emiliano Martinez: The new signing was thrown straight in, claiming two early crosses and making saves from Malick Yalcouye and Charalampos Kostoulas - though the former did beat him with a well-struck volley. He was tested again as Brighton pushed for an equaliser in the second half. 8
Wesley Fofana: Drove forward well in possession and helped pull Brighton players out of position in the build-up. 7
Maxence Lacroix: The new signing from Crystal Palace was confident in possession but not always convincing in a defensive display that was occasionally ragged. 6
Levi Colwill: Also looked comfortable on the ball but was caught out of position at times in new manager Xabi Alonso's system. 6
Pedro Neto: Tapped in Chelsea's second goal and put a chance on a plate for Joao Pedro. However, he was most at fault for over-committing to a challenge in the build-up to Brighton's first goal. 7
Malo Gusto: Played out of position in midfield. It was a quiet performance, but he delivered some good corners. 6
Romeo Lavia: After threatening to score from a similar situation in midweek, Lavia tapped in his first Chelsea goal after four minutes. 7
Jorrel Hato: The Dutchman provided a wonderful assist on the counter-attack while playing at wing-back. 7
Cole Palmer: Scored with a wonderful curling effort in the 75th minute. He pressed well but also missed a good chance early in the second half. 8
Joao Pedro: The Brazilian produced a clever flick for Chelsea's opening goal, showcased some excellent touches and made amends for missing a good chance by scoring the Blues' third. 8
Morgan Rogers: His powerful running down the flank set up Neto for Chelsea's second goal. He should have had another assist, but Palmer blazed his effort over the bar. 7
Subs:
Josh Acheampong (on 68, Fofana): Helped steady Chelsea defensively after coming on. 6
Reece James (on 68, Neto): Contributed at both ends of the pitch and provided added energy down the flank. 7
Moises Caicedo (on 68, Lavia): His afternoon was cut short after just 11 minutes as he left the pitch in tears. 6
Pep Chavarria (on 72, Colwill): An energetic cameo and looked eager to get forward. 6
Valentin Barco (on 82, Caicedo): 6
Subs not used: Penders, Gittens, Estevao Willian, Welbeck.
Brighton
Bart Verbruggen: Struggled when coming out to claim the ball for Chelsea's opening goal, but made several good saves later in the match. 5
Olivier Boscagli: Made little impact and was part of a disjointed defensive performance. 5
Lewis Dunk: Did not stand out and was involved in a lacklustre defensive display. Also fortunate to avoid greater punishment for a poor challenge on Joao Pedro. 5
Luka Vuskovic: Tested the goalkeeper with a long-range effort in the first half but looked unconvincing defensively. 5
Ferdi Kadioglu: Struggled to cope with the combination of Cole Palmer and Pedro Neto down Chelsea's right. 5
Pascal Gross: The German delivered an excellent cross to create Yalcouye's first opportunity of the game, and had the last word with his late goal. 7
Mats Wieffer: Failed to deal with an early corner, which led to a mix-up with Verbruggen and ultimately Chelsea's opener. 5
Maxim de Cuyper: Offered little attacking threat while operating in an unfamiliar advanced role because of Brighton's injury problems. 5
Malick Yalcouye: Produced an energetic display, registering Brighton's first shot before scoring with a first-time volley that went in off the post. 7
Diego Gomez: Brighton's most dangerous attacking player but also guilty of missing several chances. 5
Charalampos Kostoulas: Played a key role in Brighton's first goal after seeing an initial effort saved, but struggled to provide a consistent threat. 6
Subs:
Ibrahim Osman (on 74, Yalcouye): Made little obvious impact. 6
Costinha (on 80, Wieffer): 6
Promise David (on 80, Kostoulas): 6

summary: Chelsea secured a thrilling 4-3 victory over Brighton at Stamford Bridge in a match featuring goals from Romeo Lavia, Pedro Neto, Joao Pedro, and Cole Palmer. Brighton fought back with goals from Malick Yalcouye, a Joao Pedro own goal, and a late header from Pascal Gross. Cole Palmer's decisive strike ultimately sealed the win for the Blues.
