title: Omar Marmoush: Tottenham agree loan for Manchester City forward
author: Shamoon Hafez; Mohamed Moallim
content:
![Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/949/cpsprodpb/d37f/live/a0422f70-a125-11f1-92eb-a9b3bbcf6f4a.jpg)
Omar Marmoush has scored 16 goals in 62 games for City
- Published
Tottenham have agreed a loan deal to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush, with an obligation to make the deal permanent for Â£60m next summer.
The 27-year-old Egypt international follows Savio from City to Spurs after the north London club signed the Brazilian for an initial fee of Â£75m on Tuesday.
Marmoush joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt for Â£59m last January but had to play second fiddle to Erling Haaland for much of his time at Etihad Stadium.
He was a second-half substitute in City's 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal and then an unused substitute in their Premier League opener on Saturday, a 2-1 home win over Bournemouth.
Spurs have already spent more than Â£312m this summer on transfers.
They have signed Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton, while defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, and goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, have arrived on free transfers.
What would Marmoush give Spurs?
Marmoush scored 16 goals in 62 appearances in all competitions for City following his move from Frankfurt.
Eight of those came in 36 appearances in 2025-26, but his Premier League involvement fell considerably.
He started only eight league games and played around 700 minutes, fewer than he managed after joining midway through the prior campaign.
His league return was three goals and three assists, with his 3.53 expected goals figure close to his actual scoring output. The issue was therefore not simply finishing.
Marmoush found himself competing for minutes in a side built around Haaland, while City further strengthened their attacking options.
Spurs forward Dominic Solanke has endured injury problems over the past 18 months, while team-mate Richarlison has entered the final year of his contract.
Marmoush is primarily a number nine, but he has rarely been confined to one role across the front line.
At Frankfurt he was used predominantly through the middle but also appeared as a second striker and from the left. City have followed a similar pattern, using him mainly as a central attacker while also deploying him from the flank and just behind another forward.
That flexibility could suit Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi. His teams have often relied on forwards changing positions, dropping towards the ball and then attacking the space created when opponents are drawn out. Marmoush is comfortable doing both.
summary: Tottenham have agreed to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush on loan with an obligation to make the transfer permanent for £60m next summer. The 27-year-old Egypt international scored 16 goals in 62 appearances for City but struggled for regular playing time behind Erling Haaland. His versatility across the front line and ability to drop deep could suit the tactical approach of Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi.
key_points: Tottenham agreed a loan deal for Omar Marmoush with a £60m permanent obligation for next summer.
Marmoush scored 16 goals in 62 games for Manchester City after joining from Eintracht Frankfurt last year.
His Premier League playing time decreased significantly during the 2025-26 season as he competed with Erling Haaland.
Marmoush offers tactical flexibility, having played centrally, as a second striker, and on the flank.

title: Brydon Carse incident points to a darker truth about life as a professional cricketer | The Secret Cricket Coach
author: The Secret Cricket Coach; Guardian staff reporter
content:
I once played with a young cricketer who would physically harm himself when he didn’t score enough runs. I won’t go into the detail of how because that isn’t really the point. The point is that a young professional cricketer had reached a place where getting out in a game of cricket meant he deserved to be hurt. The strange thing is that I understood it. Not the act itself, which was obviously extreme, but the feeling behind it. Cricket meant that much to him. It meant that much to all of us.
Nobody had ever told him that his value as a person depended on how many runs he scored. Cricket had been telling him, in more subtle ways, for years. I thought about him again when I read about Brydon Carse.
I don’t know Carse and I don’t know what happened beyond what has been reported, so this isn’t really about that particular incident. It just felt familiar. Another cricketer, another night out and another conversation about why professional sportsmen can’t just behave themselves.
I didn’t drink when I played. At all. It wasn’t a moral position, I just didn’t drink, and if anything that made me unusual. Drinking was completely normal in professional cricket. I watched players who were incredibly serious about their cricket train hard, practise for hours, worry about their weight and obsess about their performances and then drink extraordinary amounts of alcohol. I could never really get my head around the contradiction. I think I understand it a little better now, because the longer I have spent around cricket the more I have wondered whether some of the things we regard as character, toughness or simply part of being a cricketer are actually ways of coping with being one.
Playing professional cricket hurts. There is the obvious physical pain. Fast bowlers spend large parts of their careers with something hurting. Batters get hit, fingers break, backs ache and knees deteriorate. Sport gives you quite a strange relationship with pain because it isn’t necessarily something that tells you to stop. Quite often it is just something you have to deal with so you can keep playing.
The mental side is probably more interesting though. Cricket is a brutal game. You can practise brilliantly all week, feel in great form and nick your first ball. You can bowl well and get smashed everywhere. You can be playing well and get left out, or playing badly and know everyone can see it. Then there are contracts, injuries, younger players coming through and coaches deciding somebody else is better. You are basically being judged all the time.
![Brydon Carse during the first Ashes Test in Perth last November](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1c69d95c801c42bdfc3badfa5c908744d3249745/0_165_2287_1570/master/2287.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
That judgment starts really young. The pathway finds the children who are better at batting and bowling and moves them on. Then it judges them again. County age group, academy, second team, professional contract, first team and eventually, for a very small number, international cricket. The level changes but the question doesn’t really: are you good enough? We talk a lot about developing people in cricket and I’m not completely convinced we do. We develop cricketers. We get better and better at teaching them to bat and bowl, preparing them physically and finding little things that might make them perform better. But ultimately the system has always had a straightforward measure of whether you are any good. Runs and wickets.
What does that do to somebody after 10 or 15 years? If you have spent most of your childhood being told that the thing that makes you different is that you are good at cricket, it seems fairly obvious that eventually some of your sense of worth gets wrapped up in being good at cricket. You get selected and you feel good. You score runs and people tell you how good you are. Then you get nought, or you get dropped, or your body breaks.
I played with some incredibly confident cricketers who were also incredibly insecure people. I used to think that was strange. I’m not sure I do any more. Maybe cricket actually creates some of that insecurity. The approval is always conditional and, however good you are, you are never that far away from someone deciding somebody else is better.
People find ways of dealing with that. Some drank. Some took drugs. Some disappeared into themselves. Some practised obsessively after failure because doing more was the only response they knew. Players played injured and pretended they weren’t. Humour covered a lot. So did bravado.
These are obviously very different behaviours with very different consequences, but I wonder whether they can sometimes perform a similar function. Something has happened that I can’t deal with, or I feel something I don’t want to feel, so I find something that changes the feeling. For one person that might mean going back into the nets. For another it might mean getting drunk. For the young player I knew it became something much darker.
Dressing rooms are incredibly funny places, but I sometimes wonder how much of that humour is also a way of making sure nobody gets too close to anything real. Looking at some aspects of dressing-room culture is a bit like switching on an episode of Little Britain now. You don’t necessarily remember being shocked by it at the time. That is almost the disturbing bit. Things become normal because everyone around you treats them as normal.
after newsletter promotion
From what I have seen in a number of cricket environments more recently, I’m not convinced the dressing room has evolved anything like as much as we like to think. The language might change and some of the more obvious excesses disappear, but the instinct to hide vulnerability is still there.
I have always been interested in the Army as a comparison. Clearly playing cricket is nothing like going to war, but there are things about the environments that I think are similar. You put groups of predominantly young people together in a fairly enclosed world. The group becomes incredibly important because often they are the only people who really understand the experience. There has been lots written about alcohol in the military and its relationship with stress, pain, belonging and coming down from intense experiences, and I wonder whether cricket has always had its own version of this.
I used to watch it happen after games. Players could spend six or seven hours completely consumed by cricket. Someone might have got nought. Someone else might have taken five wickets. Someone might have spent the day wondering whether they were ever getting back in the side. Then the day finished and they drank. Because I didn’t, perhaps I noticed the change more. People relaxed. Something that had felt disastrous two hours earlier became quite funny. The group came back together and cricket gradually disappeared.
Maybe alcohol wasn’t simply something cricketers liked doing. Maybe it actually worked. Not in a good way necessarily, but as a coping mechanism. It dulled things. Physical pain, emotional pain, anxiety, insecurity and boredom. For a few hours whatever had been bothering you bothered you a bit less. If that is part of it, I’m not sure telling players that alcohol is bad for them achieves very much. They know. An international cricketer doesn’t need another presentation explaining what alcohol does to sleep and recovery. The interesting thing is that, knowing all of that, some still choose it.
I’m just not sure we put enough effort into the person who has to live with being a cricketer. Where does identity sit in the pathway? Where do values sit? Where do we teach someone how to deal with failure when failure in cricket happens all the time? These aren’t soft things. People find ways of coping whether we help them to or not, and if we don’t give them good ones, we shouldn’t be particularly surprised when they find bad ones.
The Secret Cricket Coach is a former professional cricketer, now an elite-level coach.
summary: A former professional cricketer and elite-level coach reflects on the intense pressure, constant judgment, and physical and mental pain inherent in professional cricket. The author argues that behaviors like heavy drinking, obsessive practicing, and self-harm often serve as coping mechanisms for the deep insecurities and conditional approval fostered by the sport's environment. Ultimately, the writer suggests that the cricket system focuses heavily on developing players' skills while failing to adequately support the individuals dealing with the psychological toll of the game.
key_points: Professional cricket exposes players to constant judgment, physical pain, and the chronic stress of performance-based evaluation from a very young age.
The sport's environment often ties a player's personal self-worth directly to their on-field statistics like runs and wickets.
Behaviors such as heavy drinking, playing through injuries, and obsessive training often function as coping mechanisms for the intense pressures and insecurities of the game.
Cricket dressing rooms historically and presently encourage the hiding of vulnerability, relying on humor and bravado rather than addressing underlying emotional struggles.
The author argues that the sport needs to put more effort into developing and supporting the person behind the cricketer rather than solely focusing on physical and technical performance.

title: LASK 5-1 Celtic (agg 5-4): Hoops throw away four-goal aggregate lead as stunning collapse ends Champions League group stage hopes
author: William Bitibiri
content:
LASK 5-1 Celtic (agg 5-4): Hoops throw away four-goal aggregate lead as stunning collapse ends Champions League group stage hopes
Report as Celtic are dumped out of the Champions League after throwing away a four-goal aggregate lead to LASK; Celtic took the lead on the night through Callum McGregor but LASK scored five to deny them a spot in Thursday's draw; Celtic to play Europa League football again
Wednesday 26 August 2026 08:34, UK
Celtic suffered a stunning Champions League play-off collapse as LASK overturned a 3-0 first-leg deficit to win 5-4 after extra time and sent the Scottish champions crashing into the Europa League.
In one of the worst nights in Celtic's European history, the Hoops were up 4-0 on aggregate after Callum McGregor extended their 3-0 first-leg advantage early on in Austria.
Asked if it was the worst he's felt on the touchline, Celtic boss Martin O'Neill said: "Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the UEFA Cup final in 2003, but this was majorly disappointing."
Despite wobbling after goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic and a Samuel Adeniran stunner, Celtic were minutes from booking a place in Thursday's League phase draw before second-half substitute Florian Flecker headed home a 90th-minute equaliser to force extra time.
- How it happened | Teams | Stats
- Watch FREE Scottish Prem highlights | Latest Scottish Prem news | Latest scores
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream the Scottish Prem with no contract
Full of all the energy and desire that Celtic whimpered at the sight of, the momentum belonged to the Austrian champions. Adeniran struck from range again in the 109th minute to put LASK in front on aggregate for the first time.
He very nearly added salt to Celtic's wounds when he stepped up for a penalty moments later, after Reo Hatate fouled Krystof Danek deep, but Viljami Sinisalo kept the spot-kick out to give his side a lifeline.
It was a lifeline that went begging as the full-time whistle confirmed Celtic would miss out on the Champions League for the second consecutive season. Last season they were eliminated on penalties at this stage by Kairat Almaty.
This year's failure, given the context of a four-goal aggregate lead, will be an even harder blow.
Once again the Hoops will be involved in the Europa League league-phase draw on Friday.
The key moments from Raiffeisen Arena
- 6: BIG CHANCE! Celtic move it quickly up the field. Yang plays a ball into the area that Baur latches onto, poking wide of the mark with Hogh running in.
- 20: LASK CHANCES! The first falls to Mbuyamba in the area, who can't quite match the flight of the ball to send it goalwards. Any touch on that and Lask would have had a goal. The second has Sinisalo worried, as it strikes the post.
- 21: GOAL! It's a smart, smart low strike from McGregor but it takes a nick off Andrade and flies past Jungwirth in the LASK goal.
- 32: GOAL! IT'S A GIFT! Celtic punished for complacent play at the back. Nygren passes a ball back into no man's land, putting it on a plate for Usor to stroke past Sinisalo.
- 48: GOAL! LASK LEAD! Lask are beginning to believe. Ljubicic beats Sinisalo from range with a superb low strike from the edge of the area.
- 58: GOAL! WHAT A FINISH!!! That is simply superb technique. No chance Sinisalo was getting anywhere near that. The LASK striker is teed up outside the box and curls home.
- 90: GOAL! LASK MAKE IT FOUR TO SEND IT TO EXTRA TIME! Sinisalo does brilliantly to deny Joao Victor Tornich initially, but he can do nothing about the rebound as Florian Flecker heads home to make it 4-4 on aggregate!
- 108: GOAL! Nightmare stuff for Celtic as Adeniran strikes from range again. LASK now lead on aggregate.
- 114: FROM BAD TO WORSE! Hatate brings down Danek in the box and gives away a penalty! However, the effort is saved.
O'Neill: We should've been out of sight
Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking with Amazon Prime:
"We should've been out of sight by half-time. We missed two great opportunities and then we gave them a lifeline right before half-time and then another one just after it. They came roaring back. That's my team, that's my responsibility.
"At half-time I thought we were still well in command of the game. Just after, they score and then momentum goes in their direction. It's hard to stem it when they're chasing the game and we can't get out for 10 minutes.
"These are tough games. This might have been a qualification game but it felt like a Champions League game. That doesn't matter. Talking about the squad is for another day.
"It's a massive disappointment. We're playing in the Europa League but that's no consolation this evening. There was a feel-good factor and that's a massive disappointment tonight."
McGregor issues apology to Celtic fans
Celtic's Callum McGregor speaking with Amazon Prime:
"We got what we deserved. I thought we were passive all night. We actually looked scared to go and win the game.
"To be honest, I don't think we were that good in the first leg either and we kind of got away with it. But then you're up 3-0 and think you have a chance. When you play like that, you can't have any excuse whatsoever.
"We have to suck it up. We apologise to the supporters and to the club because there's no way we should lose that game. Now we have to see what character we have.
"You can't lose the game by such a big margin and look for excuses elsewhere. This is where we see what people are made of in terms of what we achieve this season."
How much money did Celtic throw away?
Sky Sports News' Adam Binnie:
"The big one for this is finances. Everyone will talk about the prestige and that's a big thing for Martin O'Neill - but what the club will be concerned about are the financial implications.
"£40m is the estimated total you get for qualification into the league phase of the Champions League. That's split into various parts.
"There's the UEFA Value Pillar which can add anywhere between £14m and £16m and you get at least £16m for automatic qualification no matter what happens.
"There could also be £10m added to that in gate receipts in ticket sales if Celtic were to sell out all four home matches.
"The finances are pretty drastic which has a knock-on effect. Celtic were planning on splashing the cash once again. They've spent £30m already, so where does this leave them?"
Your views: 'Celtic were hapless, hopeless and humiliated'
LJJ: "Absolutely embarrassing for Celtic, maybe Europa League is the level for them since they get into the CL with ease every year but don't make an impact when actually in it. Maybe that's their level, but I don't think they deserve Europe at all after what I've just witnessed!"
Jonny: "Celtic got what they deserved. They didn't exactly play well last week and were lucky to come away with three goals and decided to park the bus, just not good enough."
Reinaldo7: "Don't know whether to laugh or cry. Worse than last year against Kairat. Strange choices for subs tonight. Hang your heads in shame boys, they weren't that special but made us look ordinary. More work needed if we are to succeed in Europe."
Stevo: "I think this was worse than Kairat. Yes, it's not ideal losing on penalties to them, but to be 4-0 up and throw that all away, that's impressively shocking!"
jcluk: "No more LASK chances for Celtic. They were hapless, hopeless and humiliated. Can see them struggling domestically too this season."
What next for Celtic...
Celtic will play in the Europa League this season. The Europa League league phase draw - involving Bournemouth, Sunderland and Crystal Palace - takes place at 12pm UK time on Friday
summary: Celtic suffered a stunning Champions League play-off collapse, blowing a four-goal aggregate lead to lose 5-4 to LASK after extra time. Callum McGregor initially extended Celtic's 3-0 first-leg advantage in Austria, but goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic, Samuel Adeniran, and a 90th-minute header from Florian Flecker forced extra time. Adeniran then struck again in the 109th minute to complete the comeback, sending the Scottish champions crashing out of the Champions League and into the Europa League.
key_points: Celtic blew a four-goal aggregate lead against LASK to lose 5-4 after extra time in the Champions League play-offs.
Florian Flecker scored a 90th-minute equaliser for LASK to force extra time at 4-4 on aggregate.
Samuel Adeniran scored the winning goal in the 109th minute to put LASK through.
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill and captain Callum McGregor both admitted the team fell well short and offered apologies.
The defeat means Celtic will miss out on the Champions League for the second consecutive season and play in the Europa League instead.

title: Raheem Sterling could face jail time after dangerous driving and drug charges
author: Ben Rumsby
content:
![Raheem Sterling](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000407719005_17876917129960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqV7niNlA1orklOQsn0BlVNthav0Z6x0qIrC2nYozgWgM.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
![Raheem Sterling](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000407719005_17876917129960_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqV7niNlA1orklOQsn0BlVNthav0Z6x0qIrC2nYozgWgM.jpeg?imwidth=640) 
Raheem Sterling could face jail time after being charged with dangerous driving and drug offences following a motorway crash.
The former Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea forward was arrested in May this year after he was filmed swerving his £270,000 Lamborghini before colliding with barriers at around 9am on the M3 in Hampshire.
Sterling, 31, has also been charged with failing to provide a specimen following his arrest and is due to appear in court on September 15.
A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: “A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.
“Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.
“The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange, on 28 May, 2026.
“No other vehicles were involved, and no injuries were reported.”
Dangerous driving carries a maximum two-year prison sentence if found guilty. Nitrous oxide is commonly known as laughing gas, with its usage having become an issue within football. It is categorised as a Class C drug, possession of which carries a maximum prison term of two years but more often results in a fine or community service order.
![Raheem Sterling](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/content/dam/football/2026/08/25/TELEMMGLPICT000483053779_17876942708610_trans_NvBQzQNjv4BqpVlberWd9EgFPZtcLiMQf0Rf_Wk3V23H2268P_XkPxc.jpeg?imwidth=350) 
Sterling, who was released on bail following his arrest, has been without a club since his stint at Feyenoord at the end of last season after severing ties with Chelsea.
The forward previously enjoyed success at City after joining them from Liverpool in 2015, winning four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup. His subsequent move to Chelsea in 2022 coincided with a steep decline in his form.
His loan at Arsenal two seasons ago did not result in a permanent move despite being supported by Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, who had worked with him at City. Sterling was without a team this season until February, when he had a short spell in the Eredivisie.
He won 82 caps for England and played at three World Cup finals. His last game for his country was at the 2022 World Cup. He won the football writers’ player of the year and the PFA young player of the year awards in 2019.
A source close to Sterling said in May that the strain of the abrupt end to his top-level playing career had taken a toll on his well-being.
summary: Former professional footballer Raheem Sterling faces potential jail time after being charged with dangerous driving, drug possession, and failing to provide a specimen following a motorway crash in May 2026. The 31-year-old was arrested after crashing his Lamborghini on the M3 in Hampshire, with no other vehicles involved and no injuries reported. Sterling is scheduled to appear in court on September 15.
key_points: Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving, possessing nitrous oxide, and failing to provide a specimen.
The charges follow a single-vehicle crash involving his Lamborghini on the M3 in Hampshire on May 28, 2026.
No other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported.
Sterling is scheduled to appear in court on September 15 and could face up to two years in prison for dangerous driving.

title: LASK v Celtic: Martin O'Neill takes responsibility
author: Scott Mullen
content:
![Martin O'Neill takes responsibility](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/62ff/live/3a0293a0-a0dd-11f1-9eb4-25fa73e257d0.jpg)
Celtic led LASK by four goals on aggregate, before losing the tie 5-4
- Published
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.
The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.
After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.
Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.
There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.
"I'm responsible for this one," he said.
"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.
"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.
"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."
O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.
The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.
This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria.
Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.
"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.
"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.
"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.
"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."
What the players said
Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.
"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.
"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.
"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.
"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.
"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.
"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.
"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."
The pundits view
Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: "It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.
"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.
"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."
Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.
"Huge credit to LASK.
"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."
Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].
"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."
summary: Celtic suffered a historic European collapse, losing 5-4 on aggregate to LASK after squandering a four-goal aggregate lead. Manager Martin O'Neill took full responsibility for the defeat, which eliminates Celtic from the Champions League and denies the club a major financial windfall. Captain Callum McGregor and pundits admitted the team was passive, exhausted, and deserved to be knocked out.
key_points: Celtic lost 5-4 on aggregate to LASK after extra time, despite holding a four-goal aggregate lead.
Manager Martin O'Neill openly took full responsibility for the team's second-half collapse.
The elimination denies Celtic the prestige and major financial windfall associated with Champions League qualification.
Captain Callum McGregor admitted the players were passive, scared to win, and deserved the defeat.
Pundits including Scott Brown, Neil Lennon, and Stiliyan Petrov noted that LASK physically and tactically outperformed Celtic.

title: Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory
author: Jack Wilkinson
content:
Joe Root: Furious England captain 'hacked off' after Brydon Carse incident overshadows Pakistan victory
Joe Root "hacked off" by "stupid mistakes" as off-field controversy involving Brydon Carse overshadows his successful return as Test captain; watch the second England vs Pakistan Test live on Sky Sports from Thursday
Tuesday 25 August 2026 15:16, UK
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.
England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.
Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.
- England without Carse for Lord's Test after nightclub incident
- With alarm bells ringing, what's gone wrong for Pakistan cricket?
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream no contract
Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.
"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.
"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.
"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.
"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.
"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."
The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.
White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.
An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.
Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.
Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".
'We have to earn a lot of trust back'
Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.
"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.
"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.
"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.
"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."
Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.
"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.
"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.
"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

summary: England Test captain Joe Root expressed deep frustration after an off-field incident involving fast bowler Brydon Carse overshadowed the team's victory against Pakistan. Carse was withdrawn from the squad for the second Test at Lord's following a police incident in Derbyshire, prompting an investigation by the Cricket Regulator. Root acknowledged that England must eliminate repeated off-field mistakes and work to earn back the trust of the nation and its supporters.

title: US Open 2026: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz return in mixed doubles
author: Harry Poole; Russell Fuller
content:
![Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz laugh together during the US Open mixed doubles competition](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1600/cpsprodpb/6c61/live/244bbbd0-a0d4-11f1-879c-376a9fd2230d.jpg)
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz have won a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles
- Published
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.
That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.
But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.
Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.
The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.
The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.
Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.
Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."
Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.
However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.
Returning Alcaraz 'almost forgot how this feels'
While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.
The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.
"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.
"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.
"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."
For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.
"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.
"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."
![Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz are applauded by the crowd at the US Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/a08d/live/adae41c0-a0d6-11f1-b407-c570883a85b8.jpg)
Serena Williams won six of her 23 Grand Slam singles titles in New York
The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.
The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.
Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.
Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.
Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.
"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."
The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.
It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.
'The sort of semi-final line-up organisers envisaged'
Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.
With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.
Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.
But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.
The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.
This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.
summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz partnered in the US Open's revamped mixed doubles tournament, drawing a crowd of about 15,000 to Arthur Ashe Stadium. Williams was returning to the tournament for the first time since 2022, while Alcaraz was playing his first match since April due to a wrist injury. The marquee pair won their opening match before being eliminated in the quarter-finals by Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic.
key_points: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up for the US Open mixed doubles, reaching the quarter-finals.
Carlos Alcaraz was returning from a wrist injury that sidelined him for nearly five months.
Serena Williams played at Flushing Meadows for the first time since stepping away from tennis in 2022.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format features top singles stars alongside traditional doubles players.
Williams and Alcaraz were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Italy's Flavio Cobolli and Switzerland's Belinda Bencic.

- Published
Enjoy it - and do what Serena Williams tells you to.
That was how Carlos Alcaraz settled back into competitive action at the US Open, partnering the American great as she returned to her home slam after a four-year absence.
The tournament's revamped mixed doubles format has attracted criticism for favouring the allure of the sport's top singles stars at the expense of established doubles players.
But the crowds turned out and produced a terrific atmosphere for the tournament's headline act, with about 15,000 people packed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium.
All four doubles specialist pairings lost to a team of singles players on Tuesday, while Alcaraz and Williams fell in the quarter-finals.
Seven-time major winner Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April after injuring his wrist, while 23-time Grand Slam champion Williams was competing in New York for the first time since she "evolved away" from tennis in 2022.
The pair were greeted by huge cheers and were roared on throughout their opening 5-3 4-1 win against Great Britain's Lloyd Glasspool and New Zealand's Erin Routliffe.
The 44-year-old Williams won the US Open mixed doubles title in its original format alongside Max Mirnyi in 1998 - five years before Alcaraz was born.
Almost 30 years later, Williams still had the competitive desire. She and Alcaraz enjoyed the occasion, playing with smiles on their faces and roaring each other on after winning a point.
Interviewed during a change of ends, Alcaraz said: "I'm playing next to the one and only Serena Williams, so what else can I do? Just enjoy and try to do the things she told me to do."
Their partnership improved rapidly in their first match as they won eight of the final nine games to seal victory.
However, they were denied a place in Wednesday's semi-finals by Italy's world number six Flavio Cobolli and Swiss team-mate Belinda Bencic, who won 5-4 (7-4) 4-1.
Returning Alcaraz 'almost forgot how this feels'
While Williams will not contest the singles at the US Open - she has not competed in that format since injuring her knee at Wimbledon - Tuesday's matches provided the returning Alcaraz with valuable court time.
The Spaniard admitted he felt nervous before stepping out on the court - in part due to partnering six-time US Open women's singles champion Williams.
"I think everyone could see I was really nervous, I double-faulted on the first point," Alcaraz said after their opening win.
"I was out for almost five months and I almost forgot how it feels stepping out on the court once again.
"It [took] just a couple of games [to settle] and she made it very easy for me to enjoy it and try to go for it."
For Williams, a return to the Arthur Ashe Stadium was something she did not believe would come around again.
"It's always amazing to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said.
"It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."
![Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz are applauded by the crowd at the US Open](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/ace/standard/1024/cpsprodpb/a08d/live/adae41c0-a0d6-11f1-b407-c570883a85b8.jpg)
Serena Williams won six of her 23 Grand Slam singles titles in New York
The controversial revamped mixed doubles format, introduced last year, pits established doubles players against some of the sport's biggest singles stars.
The tournament takes place the week before the singles draw gets under way and allows direct entry into the main draw for top-ranked singles players and wildcards.
Established doubles players such as Britons Glasspool and Henry Patten had to come through two qualifying rounds on Monday.
Top-ranked players Patten and Katerina Siniakova advanced to the quarter-finals before losing to husband-and-wife duo Gael Monfils and Elina Svitolina.
Discussing their dynamic, with a semi-final against Cobolli and Bencic to come, Frenchman Monfils said: "I'm a big fan of her game and mentality. Sometimes I think she's ice and I'm the fire.
"We needed to the find the balance. We did today."
The other semi-final will see Russians Mirra Andreeva and Andrey Rublev face Czech pair Karolina Muchova and Jakub Mensik.
It was not all plain sailing for the leading singles players, with men's 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic and women's world number one Aryna Sabalenka suffering an early exit at the hands of Patten and Siniakova.
'The sort of semi-final line-up organisers envisaged'
Sabalenka and Djokovic lasted just 49 minutes, but this was otherwise a day where the singles stars edged out the doubles specialists.
With none of the four doubles pairs making it to the last four, the USTA has the sort of semi-final line up it envisaged when deciding to reinvent the mixed doubles 12 months ago.
Sabalenka and Djokovic turned out to be a very brief experiment. The other marquee pairing of Williams and Alcaraz lasted longer, with Williams in particular catching the eye in their first round win.
But with Alcaraz looking increasingly rusty in the quarter-final, Cobolli and Bencic won convincingly.
The Spaniard was wearing a compression sleeve on his right arm, and the skin fade of earlier in the year has been replaced by a mop of black hair.
This was useful court time for him, but did not really tell us anything about his chances of remaining in New York for the singles final in just under three weeks time.
summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz partnered in the US Open's revamped mixed doubles tournament, drawing a crowd of about 15,000 to Arthur Ashe Stadium. Williams was returning to the tournament for the first time since 2022, while Alcaraz was playing his first match since April due to a wrist injury. After winning their opening match, the pair were eliminated in the quarter-finals by Italy's Flavio Cobolli and Switzerland's Belinda Bencic.
key_points: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up for the US Open mixed doubles event, winning their opening match before exiting in the quarter-finals.
The tournament featured a controversial revamped format favoring top singles stars, with all four specialist doubles pairings losing to singles player teams on Tuesday.
Carlos Alcaraz was playing his first competitive match since April following a wrist injury.
Serena Williams competed at her home slam for the first time since moving away from tennis in 2022.
Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic defeated Williams and Alcaraz 5-4 (7-4) 4-1 to reach the semi-finals.

title: US Open LIVE: Latest scores and updates as Williams and Alcaraz play mixed doubles
author: Flo Clifford
content:
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles tournament but were knocked out by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
23-time grand slam champion Williams was competing in New York four years after the final competitive singles match of her career - or at least, the first phase of her career - before she began “evolving away” from the sport.
But the 44-year-old returned to action alongside Spaniard Alcaraz, who had not played in four months due to a troublesome wrist injury - but is back to defend his singles title at Flushing Meadows.
Elsewhere in the high-profile but controversial mixed doubles event, which is in its second year after a major revamp, world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka and 24-time grand slam champion Novak Djokovic were made top seeds but were knocked out in the first round by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
Follow all the action with our liveblog below:
Bencic/Cobolli see off Williams/Alcaraz
Another entertaining encounter goes the way of the fourth seeds.
So our semi-final line-ups are almost set:
Belinda Bencic/Flavio Cobolli v Elina Svitolina/Gael Monfils
Karolina Muchova/Jakub Mensik v Mirra Andreeva/Andrey Rublev OR Diana Shnaider/Casper Ruud
![](https://static.independent.co.uk/2026/08/25/23/2026-08-25T220314Z_1573894166_UP1EM8P1P9CCB_RTRMADP_3_TENNIS-USOPEN.JPG)
GAME, SET AND MATCH! Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 4-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Alcaraz goes long on the return, and the smiles finally come out for Bencic and Cobolli!
They’re into the semi-finals, where they’ll face Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils.
Smiles too for Williams and Alcaraz, who have shaken some of the rust off with those two matches today.
*Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 3-1 Williams/Alcaraz
So, Cobolli will face for a place in the semi-finals. Bencic knocks a net volley right at Alcaraz’s feet to push him off-balance for 15-0. Then Alcaraz goes wide on a tricky second serve.
Williams nets on a backhand, and that’s four match points...
BREAK! *Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 3-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Very assured by Bencic at the baseline as she trades blows with Alcaraz, before Williams intercepts - but goes long. 15-15 on the Alcaraz serve.
Cobolli reacts brilliantly to lash a Williams drop shot cross-court, leaving Bencic acres of space to hammer in the winner.
Williams gets a smash away for 30-30, but a great return by Cobolli brings up break point chance... an ace saves the first, but they’ll have another.
Ooh, Cobolli reads it well, and Alcaraz goes long!
Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 2-1 Williams/Alcaraz*
Williams is just producing a few more unforced errors than in the earlier match against Routliffe and Glasspool. She nets on a weak Bencic second serve, and Alcaraz slams the tape too under pressure from Cobolli.
The Italian lets a Williams volley drop and waits, then plants it into the open court.
*Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 1-1 Williams/Alcaraz
Williams smiles ruefully as she nets and a chorus of support comes up from Arthur Ashe. The decibels from the American have gone up too.
From 0-30 down Alcaraz pushes Cobolli back and fires an overhead into the open court, and an ace down the T from Williams gets them to parity.
Cobolli draws the error from Williams in a cross-court rally and that gives them two break points... Bencic is unlucky that a return drifts wide for deuce.
Alcaraz seals the deciding point at the net!
Bencic/Cobolli 5-4, 1-0 Williams/Alcaraz*
Cobolli is in a spot of bother on serve but Williams hammers a forehand into the net as the Italian goes up 40-30.
He whacks a forehand into the open court and seals the hold. Both teams are so comfortable at the back of the court.
GAME AND FIRST SET! Bencic/Cobolli 5-4 Williams/Alcaraz
Cobolli smashes away after Bencic pounces on a weaker Williams second serve for 4-4.
And Williams goes long at the baseline! 5-4... Cobolli can serve this out now.
Williams mishits a wild volley and that gives Cobolli two set points!
A kick serve out wide seals it. The pair exchange a businesslike high five. Serious stuff.
Bencic/Cobolli 4-4 Williams/Alcaraz*
Big serving by Cobolli to build a 3-0 lead.
Bencic nets on Alcaraz’s serve... and Williams powers away a smash at the net to close some of the gap.
She does so again, and that lead evaporates. 3-3.
summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz reached the quarter-finals of the US Open mixed doubles tournament before being knocked out by fourth seeds Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli. Williams returned to competition in New York four years after her last competitive singles match, while Alcaraz returned following a four-month wrist injury. In another notable first-round match, top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were eliminated by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
key_points: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz were defeated in the US Open mixed doubles quarter-finals by Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli.
Bencic and Cobolli advanced to the semi-finals to face Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils.
Top seeds Aryna Sabalenka and Novak Djokovic were knocked out in the first round by Katerina Siniakova and Henry Patten.
The tournament marked Williams' return to competitive tennis in New York four years after her final singles match.

title: Leeds player ratings vs Forest as 'assured' debutant gets 8/10 but 'sloppy' 5
author: Kyle Newbould
content:
Leeds United booked their place in the Carabao Cup third round after beating Nottingham Forest 2-0 on Tuesday night. A second-half goal from Daniel James and a Neco Williams own-goal sent Daniel Farke’s side home from the City Ground with a second win in four days.
Chances fell at both ends during the first-half, the biggest for Chris Wood who after nutmegging Nico Elvedi, was primed to finish but for a goal-saving Joe Rodon tackle. Sean Longstaff had Leeds’ best opportunity after James got free down the right, but the midfielder was falling as he shot and a weak effort was collected by Matz Sels.
James opened the scoring six minutes into the second-half, finishing well beyond Sels and into the far corner after Longstaff pounced on some loose Forest play. And Williams put into his own net to double the away side’s lead with around 15 minutes remaining, although James Justin might be trying to claim it as his own.

Daniel James scored the opening goal six minutes into the second half.

title: Celtic throw away four-goal aggregate lead to crash out of Champions League against Lask
author: PA Media; Guardian staff reporter
content:
Celtic threw away a four-goal lead in Austria as they missed out on the Champions League for the second year running. The Scottish champions looked to be cruising into the league stage when Callum McGregor put them 4-0 up on aggregate against Lask with a 21st-minute deflected strike.
However, they went on to endure one of their all-time European lows with a 5-1 defeat in Linz delivering a £20m-plus blow.
The Hoops had other chances in the first half but the Austrians gave themselves a lifeline when Moses Usor pounced on a loose pass from Benjamin Nygren to level on the night in the 32nd minute.
The tie began to spiral out of Celtic’s control early in the second half as Robert Ljubicic and Samuel Adeniran netted from outside the box. Martin O’Neill’s side looked like they would cling on but Florian Flecker nodded home from close range in stoppage-time to spark an additional 30 minutes.
Celtic had disappeared as an attacking force at half-time and Adeniran delivered the knockout blow that sends them into the Europa League.
The Hoops exited on penalties at the playoff stage last season after failing to sign a proven striker before drawing a blank against Kairat Almaty. Fans will this year question the decision to sell Arne Engels just ahead of the first leg after they lost control in midfield in Austria.
The quality of Celtic’s finishing had been the difference in Glasgow but Lask created chances throughout and the second leg started in similar fashion.
Celtic looked to extend their lead. Mika Baur stabbed an early chance just wide and Kasper Høgh forced a couple of first-half saves from decent opportunities. McGregor opened the scoring in between those chances when he drilled a first-time shot in off a defender after Yang Hyun-jun had played a one-two with Kieran Tierney.
The home side had exerted some pressure just before McGregor’s goal and they levelled following careless play from Nygren. The Austrian champions pulled a goal back three minutes after the restart when Usor outmuscled Auston Trusty and worked the ball inside for Ljubicic to drive home from 20 yards.
![Dismayed Celtic players react to their capitulation](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/9dae202d24604a80213dda2cac29b8f00d1f617f/0_0_4199_2799/master/4199.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)
Celtic endured some nervy moments before they conceded again in the 58th minute when Adeniran curled a wonderful first-time strike into the top corner from 25 yards.
after newsletter promotion
Celtic were on the ropes. Several shots flew past Viljami Sinisalo’s goal before the Finn pulled off a great stop from Sascha Horvath. João Victor Tornich headed inches wide from the resulting corner.
Adeniran fired off the underside of the bar and Celtic defended with four centre-backs as Liam Scales and Dane Murray came on to join Trusty and Cameron Carter-Vickers.
With Luke McCowan, Reo Hatate and Sebastian Tounekti also off the bench, Carter-Vickers had to struggle on with cramp and Celtic could not hold out. Sinisalo made a great stop from a Tornich header but Flecker converted the rebound.
Anthony Ralston replaced Carter-Vickers as extra-time allowed O’Neill to make a further change and Celtic appeared to stem the tide. However, Adeniran fired home from 25 yards with five minutes left after dispossessing McCowan and Celtic could not threaten after Sinisalo’s penalty save denied the striker his hat-trick.
summary: Celtic squandered a four-goal aggregate lead to suffer a 5-1 defeat against Lask in Austria, resulting in a Champions League exit. Callum McGregor had initially put Celtic ahead in the 21st minute, but goals from Moses Usor, Robert Ljubicic, Florian Flecker, and two from Samuel Adeniran turned the tie around. The defeat deals a £20m-plus financial blow to Celtic and drops them into the Europa League.
key_points: Celtic lost 5-1 on the night in Linz after holding a 4-0 aggregate lead.
Samuel Adeniran scored two goals for Lask, including the knockout blow in extra time.
Florian Flecker forced extra time by scoring in stoppage time at the end of regulation.
The defeat marks the second consecutive year Celtic has missed out on the Champions League.

title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
author: Guardian sport
content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.
Baleba has signed a five-year contract with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.
Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer when Casemiro left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.
“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.
“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.
“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”
United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-old a week ago.
United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.
after newsletter promotion
“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.”
summary: Manchester United has completed the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m on a five-year contract. He is the club's third midfield addition of the summer, following Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans, bringing United's total summer midfield spending to approximately £148m. The move comes after Casemiro's departure and a serious knee injury to Manuel Ugarte.
key_points: Carlos Baleba signed a five-year contract with an option for an extra 12 months.
The transfer fee is £65m plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on clause.
Baleba joins Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans as United's summer midfield recruits.
The new signings elevate Manchester United's total midfield spending to about £148m.

title: Delap heads to Forest for £50m as Chelsea open talks to sell Jackson to Aston Villa
author: Jacob Steinberg
content:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a deal worth £50m to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, who have also opened talks over selling Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa.
Xabi Alonso has made João Pedro and Danny Welbeck his main strikers this season, leaving his other frontmen to seek opportunities elsewhere.
Forest were one of several clubs interested in Delap, who has struggled since joining Chelsea from Ipswich for £30m last summer, and will pay a club record of £45m plus £5m in add-ons for the 23-year-old.
Delap managed only one league goal last season and was hindered by injuries after leaving Ipswich. But the former Manchester City striker was a key target for Forest’s manager, Oliver Glasner, and has a chance to revive his career at the City Ground.
Chelsea are focused on outgoings before the transfer window shuts next Tuesday and are also hoping to sell Jackson, who was on loan at Bayern Munich last season. The Senegal international is valued at £65m and has been earmarked by Villa as a potential replacement for Ollie Watkins, who is expected to join the Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.
Chelsea are not willing to agree to another loan for Jackson and want his valuation met but Villa are likely to press for a favourable payment schedule to ensure they can afford a permanent deal. Atlético Madrid are also interested in the 25-year-old, who joined Chelsea from Villarreal in 2023. Unai Emery, Villa’s manager, worked with Jackson at Villarreal.
West Ham’s clear out after relegation from the Premier League is expected to continue with El Hadji Malick Diouf joining Brentford for about £35m. The clubs are in discussions over a deal for the left-back and an agreement is likely soon.
Diouf wants to leave and was left out of the squad when Nuno Espírito Santo’s side continued their disappointing start to the Championship season by losing 2-1 at home against Charlton last Saturday.
West Ham signed the Senegal international for £19m from Slavia Prague last year. Brentford have made four signings and are plan to strengthen further.
after newsletter promotion
Nuno, who is understood to be under growing pressure after West Ham’s flat start, has had his hand weakened by a host of players hoping to force their way out. The Mexico midfielder Edson Álvarez has not been involved in the first two league games and is the subject of interest from Olympiakos and Real Sociedad.
Torino have had a bid rejected for the midfielder Soungoutou Magassa, who is on Crystal Palace’s shortlist. Marseille could sign the French centre-back Jean-Clair Todibo. West Ham have raised funds through the sales of Mateus Fernandes, Crysencio Summerville and Freddie Potts, and have loaned Aaron Wan-Bissaka to Aston Villa and Niclas Füllkrug to Werder Bremen.
summary: Nottingham Forest has agreed to a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea, while Chelsea has also opened talks to sell Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa for £65m. Meanwhile, West Ham continues a player clear-out following their relegation, with El Hadji Malick Diouf in talks to join Brentford for about £35m. Other West Ham players, including Edson Álvarez, are also drawing interest from various clubs as manager Nuno Espírito Santo faces mounting pressure.
key_points: Nottingham Forest agreed to a £50m deal (comprising £45m plus £5m in add-ons) to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea.
Chelsea is in talks to sell Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa for £65m as Villa seeks a replacement for Ollie Watkins.
West Ham left-back El Hadji Malick Diouf is close to joining Brentford for approximately £35m.
West Ham manager Nuno Espírito Santo is under growing pressure following a poor start in the Championship and multiple players seeking exits.

title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
author: Adrian Kajumba; Sahil Jaidka
content:
Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences
Tuesday 25 August 2026 18:34, UK
Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.
York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.
York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.
He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.
Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.
Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.
"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.
"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."
The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.
They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.
When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.
A San Francisco 49ers statement read: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."
The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.
Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.
summary: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested on Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio. He pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after prosecutors amended an initial charge of engaging in prostitution. York was sentenced to one day in jail, which was already served, and fined $1,150.
key_points: Jed York was arrested at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio.
He pleaded no contest to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.
Prosecutors amended the original charge of engaging in prostitution.
York received a one-day jail sentence, which was credited as served, and a $1,150 fine.
The NFL stated it is aware of the arrest and will review the matter under its personal conduct policy.
